justifications.type_expressiveness: Good use of enums for Expr, Value, BinOp, UnaryOp, and EvalError variants, but TypeError carries a String message instead of a structured variant and ParseError uses a String message field rather than typed kinds.
justifications.error_handling: Typed error enums with the three required EvalError variants and no panics in library paths, but TypeError/ParseError messages are stringly-typed and there are some unreachable!() arms (justified but undocumented).
justifications.api_ergonomics: Public API is clean and Display/Debug are implemented where required, but there are no doc comments on any public item, ParseError.message/offset are public fields, and EvalError lacks PartialEq and a std::error::Error impl.
justifications.idiomaticity: Generally idiomatic with ?, matches!, and recursive descent, but the env is a Vec scanned linearly with String clones on lookup and manual Debug impls duplicate what derive would produce.
